tagline: See what a command will change before it runs

cost.summary: Off by default, no model call. The `Explain with Haiku` setting turns on a plain-language explanation from Haiku for each held command.
readme: By default this mod makes no model call: the held dialog shows only the rule's reason and the preview.

Turn on Explain with Haiku (`/mod-blast-radius settings`) and each held command is sent to Haiku for a plain-language explanation, so the command text leaves your machine like any prompt. That spends tokens and counts against your plan quota. It is off by default.

features.title: Hold
features.detail: A risky Bash command waits before it runs, with no timeout: rm, git reset --hard, force push, SQL DROP, production deploys, gcloud, az, databricks, chmod 777, curl into a shell, credential reads, mv over a file, > over a file and Windows deletes.

features.title: Your rules
features.detail: ~/.claude/mods-data/mod-blast-radius/rules.json, an array of { "pattern": "regex", "reason": "text", "flags": "i" }. Read again when the file changes. A bad entry is skipped with a note in the settings pane; the built-in checks never depend on it.

features.title: Pass rules
features.detail: An entry with "action": "pass" lets a matching step through without a hold, so your other hooks and permissions decide it. Each step of a command is matched on its own, so `rm a.txt && rm -rf ~` passes the first step and still holds the second. Example: { "pattern": "^\\s*rm(?!.*\\s(-[a-zA-Z]*[rR][a-zA-Z]*|--recursive)(\\s|$))\\s", "reason": "Plain rm is decided elsewhere", "action": "pass" } lets rm without -r through. Without "action", or with "hold", an entry adds a hold as before. A pass never lets these through, whatever the pattern: a target at the root, at home (~ or $HOME), in a parent folder (..) or on a whole drive; a recursive delete of a critical folder (.git, .github, .claude, .vscode, src, helpers, resources, tests, scripts, fixtures); a step that hands text to a shell (bash -c, eval, powershell -Command); and a step with a command substitution ($(...) or backticks).

features.title: No drawing surface
features.detail: Where nothing can show the hold (a VS Code chat panel, claude -p, an SDK session), the call is not held. The permission system asks instead, with the reason.

features.title: Preview
features.detail: Paths with counts and size, git status and dry runs, the commits a force push would drop. Read-only: the command itself never runs.

features.title: Run or Cancel
features.detail: Cancel refuses the call with a reason Claude reads. A narrow terminal draws the same report above the prompt.

features.title: Show all
features.detail: The card shows two rows of its sentence. Show all on the card opens the whole sentence, and Show less folds it back.

features.title: This session's permission checks
features.detail: The card counts the session's permission checks and how many were denied. Details ends with one cell per check (allowed, asked, denied, waiting, or made by a subagent) and the counts by file, shell and other tools. Secrets in a command are masked before anything is kept, and /clear starts the list again. The mod only watches these checks; it never changes their answer.

spans.text: runs at once, nothing is held
runs at once, nothing is held
